title: Hanani Reports Jerusalem's Distress
image_prompt: In the Persian royal city of Shushan, Nehemiah, cupbearer to King Artaxerxes, receives visitors from Judah, including Hanani. They report that the returned remnant is in great trouble and reproach, Jerusalem's wall is broken down, and its gates have been burned. Show Nehemiah listening beside the royal residence, travelers dusty from the road, and a scroll or simple drawing of ruined Jerusalem. The mood is serious, with no modern objects.

title: Nehemiah Fastens His Heart in Prayer
image_prompt: Nehemiah sits down, weeps, mourns, fasts, and prays before the God of heaven. His prayer confesses Israel's sins, recalls God's covenant mercy, asks Him to hear the prayers of His servants, and requests favor before the king. Show Nehemiah kneeling in a quiet chamber at dawn, royal cupbearer's clothing nearby, a lamp and scroll on a low table, and the beginning of resolve in his expression.

title: Nehemiah Asks the King for Permission
image_prompt: Nehemiah serves wine to Artaxerxes, who notices his sadness. Nehemiah explains Jerusalem's ruin and asks to be sent to rebuild the city; he requests letters for governors and timber from the keeper of the king's forest. The king grants the requests, and Nehemiah attributes the favor to God's good hand. Show the Persian audience chamber, the king on a raised seat, Nehemiah respectfully presenting his request, and sealed documents prepared by scribes.

title: Nehemiah Encounters Opposition
image_prompt: Nehemiah travels with the king's letters and officers of the army and horsemen. Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official are displeased that someone has come to seek Israel's welfare. Show the caravan entering the region near Jerusalem while the two opponents observe from a distance, their expressions guarded and hostile; the scene foreshadows opposition without depicting an attack.

title: Nehemiah Inspects Jerusalem by Night
image_prompt: After arriving, Nehemiah rests for three days, then goes out at night with a few men and no public announcement. He examines the broken walls and burned gates, riding a beast through the Valley Gate toward the Dragon Well and Dung Gate, and finds some places too ruined to pass. Show moonlit rubble, collapsed masonry, charred gate beams, Nehemiah holding a lantern, and a small, discreet inspection party; no officials or residents know his full plan yet.

title: Nehemiah Calls the People to Rebuild
image_prompt: Nehemiah tells Jerusalem's leaders and people about the distress and explains how the king supported the mission. They answer, 'Let us rise up and build.' Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem mock them, but Nehemiah declares that the God of heaven will prosper the work. Show Nehemiah addressing the assembled families among the broken wall, people lifting tools, and opponents watching from outside.

title: Priests, Families, and Local Leaders Repair the Northern and Western Sections
image_prompt: The high priest Eliashib and fellow priests rebuild the Sheep Gate and dedicate it; other groups repair nearby stretches, including the men of Jericho, Zaccur, Meremoth, Meshullam, Zadok, Tekoites, and Shallum with his daughters. Show different households rebuilding adjacent wall sections with stone baskets, wooden beams, mortar, and gates, the repaired work joined section by section. This is a coordinated reconstruction montage that honors the named workers without pretending every person occupies the same exact spot.

title: The Valley Gate, Dung Gate, and Southern Wall
image_prompt: The people of Zanoah repair the Valley Gate and the wall toward the Dung Gate; Malchiah works on the Dung Gate, Shallun on the Fountain Gate, and Nehemiah son of Azbuk repairs a section opposite the tombs of David and toward the pool. Show crews handling heavy gate timbers, hauling stones, and clearing debris near pools and tombs. Use Jerusalem's rugged topography to distinguish sections of the wall.

title: The Eastern and Upper Sections Are Rebuilt
image_prompt: Meremoth, priests, Benjamin and Hashub, Azariah, Binnui, and other named workers repair the remaining lengths, including the area by the house of Eliashib and the Water Gate, Horse Gate, and inspection gate. Goldsmiths, merchants, and residents work near their own homes, while the priests repair the stretch above their houses. Show the wall nearly encircling Jerusalem, each team at a marked section, with the Temple Mount in the distance.

title: Sanballat and Tobiah Mock the Builders
image_prompt: Sanballat becomes angry and mocks the Jews' work, asking whether weak people can rebuild the wall or revive burned stones. Tobiah jokes that even a fox could break their stone wall. Nehemiah prays, and the people continue building until the wall reaches half its height because they have a mind to work. Show the opponents speaking from a ridge, builders lifting stones in the foreground, and a substantial new wall rising behind them.

title: The Threat of a Coordinated Attack
image_prompt: Sanballat, Tobiah, Arabs, Ammonites, and Ashdodites conspire to attack Jerusalem and create confusion. Nehemiah and the people pray and set a watch day and night. Nehemiah addresses the nobles and leaders, urging them not to fear but to remember the great LORD and defend their families. Show watchmen on the wall, scouts observing the surrounding hills, families gathered near work sections, and weapons kept ready.

title: Builders Work with Weapons at Hand
image_prompt: When the enemies learn that their plan is known, the people return to work. Half the servants work while half hold spears, shields, bows, and armor; builders keep a sword at their side, and a trumpeter stays near Nehemiah to signal danger. The people lodge within Jerusalem and remain ready to respond. Show a disciplined worksite where masons lay stone, guards stand behind them, and a trumpet bearer watches for signals; avoid anachronistic weapons.

title: A Crisis of Debt and Hunger
image_prompt: Men and women cry out against fellow Jews because families lack grain, mortgage fields and vineyards, borrow money for taxes, and see children threatened by debt servitude. Show hungry households, parents speaking anxiously at a communal gathering, and field deeds or debt records in the hands of creditors. The scene is empathetic and non-sensational, emphasizing a crisis within the community during the wall's construction.

title: Nehemiah Confronts the Nobles
image_prompt: Nehemiah becomes angry when he hears of exploitation, consults with himself, and rebukes the nobles and rulers for charging interest and burdening their kin. He calls for restoration of fields, vineyards, oliveyards, houses, and the interest already taken. The leaders agree, and Nehemiah calls priests to witness the pledge, shaking out his garment as a symbolic warning. Show a public meeting with debtors and nobles facing one another, followed by written promises of restitution.

title: Nehemiah Refuses to Exploit His Office
image_prompt: As governor, Nehemiah does not claim the food allowance of former governors; he feeds many at his own table and refuses to burden the people, because the work is heavy and the people are already distressed. Show a generous but modest communal meal with officials, visitors, and workers, Nehemiah serving and sharing rather than displaying luxury. His closing prayer asks God to remember his good deeds.

title: Sanballat Tries to Lure Nehemiah Away
image_prompt: With the wall nearly complete, Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem, and others repeatedly invite Nehemiah to meet in the plain of Ono, intending harm. Nehemiah refuses to abandon the great work, replying that he is doing a great work and cannot come down. They send a threatening letter accusing him of planning to rebel and become king; Nehemiah denies the false charge and prays for strength. Show repeated messengers at Jerusalem's gate and Nehemiah continuing to supervise masonry.

title: A False Prophet Attempts to Intimidate Nehemiah
image_prompt: Shemaiah urges Nehemiah to hide in the Temple because people are coming to harm him, but Nehemiah refuses to violate the sanctuary's rules or flee. He recognizes that Tobiah and Sanballat have hired prophets to frighten him. Show a private meeting in a house with a doorway suggesting the Temple precinct beyond, Nehemiah standing resolute, and the trap exposed through wary expressions rather than supernatural effects.

title: The Wall Is Finished Amid Continuing Intrigue
image_prompt: The wall is completed in fifty-two days, astonishing the surrounding nations, who recognize that the work has been done with God's help. Yet nobles of Judah maintain correspondence with Tobiah through family ties and continue reporting Nehemiah's words to him. Show the complete wall and gates, citizens celebrating on top of the ramparts, neighboring leaders looking on in surprise, and a quieter foreground detail of sealed letters illustrating that political tension remains.

title: Nehemiah Appoints Gatekeepers and Plans for the City
image_prompt: After the wall is built, Nehemiah sets doors in place and appoints gatekeepers, singers, and Levites. He entrusts Jerusalem's charge to Hanani and Hananiah, a faithful man who fears God, and orders the gates to remain closed until the sun is hot, with guards stationed and each resident assigned a watch near home. The city is large but sparsely populated and many houses are not yet rebuilt. Show the repaired walls surrounding open areas and scattered homes, watch rotations being organized at the gates.

title: The Register of Returning Families
image_prompt: God puts it into Nehemiah's heart to gather the nobles, rulers, and people for genealogical registration. A lengthy record lists those who first returned under Zerubbabel, including family groups such as Parosh, Shephatiah, Arah, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, Zaccai, Bani, Bebai, Azgad, Adonikam, Bigvai, Adin, Ater, Bezai, Jorah, Hashum, and others. Show a scribe's broad register with household delegates standing by their ancestral markers, travel-worn families, and the restored city as backdrop; the names should remain the primary information.

title: Priests, Levites, Singers, Gatekeepers, and Temple Servants
image_prompt: The register separately identifies priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, Nethinim, and descendants of Solomon's servants. Show these groups gathered in clearly differentiated rows: priests in plain service garments, musicians with lyres and cymbals, gatekeepers beside a gate, and temple servants carrying supplies. The visual should make their roles clear without adding ceremonial actions not stated in the record.

title: Families Whose Genealogy Is Uncertain
image_prompt: Some returnees cannot show their father's house or prove their Israelite lineage, and certain priestly families are excluded from priestly office until a priest can consult the Urim and Thummim. Show families presenting worn records to the registry officials, who carefully record uncertainty rather than inventing ancestry. A priest stands nearby with his sacred garment, emphasizing the seriousness of priestly eligibility.

title: The Community's Numbers and Gifts
image_prompt: The whole congregation totals 42,360, together with servants and singers; the record notes their animals and the gifts of family heads toward the work. The people settle in their towns, with some priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, and temple servants living in Jerusalem. Show households dividing toward villages, animals and goods unloaded, and leaders making final entries in the census scroll.

title: Ezra Reads the Law before the Assembly
image_prompt: In the seventh month, all the people gather in the square before the Water Gate and ask Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses. Ezra stands on a wooden platform; he opens the scroll where all can see, and the people rise. Levites including Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, and others help the people understand the reading. Show a vast crowd of men and women and all who can understand, morning sunlight over the square, and the scroll as the central object.

title: The People Weep, Then Rejoice
image_prompt: Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites tell the people not to mourn because the day is holy to the LORD. The people are moved by hearing the law, but they are directed to eat rich food, drink sweet drink, and send portions to those who have nothing prepared. They go away to rejoice because they understand the words. Show tears changing to relief, shared food and drink, and neighbors carrying portions to absent or poor households.

title: The Feast of Booths Is Celebrated
image_prompt: On the second day, family heads, priests, and Levites gather with Ezra to study the law and discover the command to dwell in booths during the feast. The people gather branches from olive, wild olive, myrtle, palm, and other leafy trees to build temporary shelters on roofs, courtyards, and public squares. They celebrate the feast and read the law each day. Show Jerusalem's roofs and courtyards dotted with leafy booths, families dwelling together, and daily public reading of Scripture.

title: The People Fast and Confess
image_prompt: On the twenty-fourth day of the month, the Israelites gather with fasting, sackcloth, and earth upon them. They separate from foreign practices, read from the book of the law for part of the day, and confess their sins and the iniquities of their ancestors. The Levites call the people to stand and bless the LORD. Show a solemn assembly at the square, scrolls being read, and worshippers humbly bowed, without portraying ethnicity itself as a moral defect.

title: The Prayer Recalls Creation and the Exodus
image_prompt: The Levites lead a long prayer recounting that the LORD made heaven and earth, chose Abram and named him Abraham, saw Israel's affliction in Egypt, divided the sea, led the people with cloud and fire, spoke at Sinai, and provided manna and water in the wilderness. Show a respectful sequence of visual memories—stars and sea, Abraham's tent, the Exodus crossing, Sinai, the wilderness camp—framed by the present-day assembly listening to the prayer.

title: Israel's Rebellion and God's Patience
image_prompt: The prayer recounts the people's pride and disobedience in the wilderness, the golden calf, God's continued mercy, the gift of land, and the victories and abundance the people received. Present the golden calf as a past failure, then the pillar of cloud and fire, manna, and cultivated land, with the worshipping assembly in the foreground. Use a montage that clearly distinguishes remembered events across generations.

title: Cycles of Rebellion, Oppression, and Deliverance
image_prompt: The prayer describes Israel rejecting the law, ignoring prophets, and falling under foreign nations, then crying out and receiving deliverers because God is merciful. Repeated cycles are shown as linked historical vignettes: warning prophets, fortified cities under threat, prayerful people, and temporary peace. The final words acknowledge that God has been just while the people remain under foreign kings. Keep the sequence broad and avoid inventing specific judges or events not named here.

title: The Community Enters a Written Covenant
image_prompt: The prayer asks God to remember the people's distress and acknowledges that kings, priests, and ancestors have suffered under foreign rulers. The people pledge a binding covenant in writing, signed by leaders and sealed as a public commitment. Show scribes preparing a large document, leaders pressing seals, and the gathered community standing solemnly beside it.

title: The Covenant Signatories
image_prompt: A long list names the leaders who seal the covenant, including Nehemiah the governor, Zedekiah, priests, Levites, and chiefs of the people. Show a formal signing scene with each family representative taking a turn, and a parchment register identifying priestly and lay groups. Do not invent personal traits or dialogue for those named only in the list.

title: The People Pledge to Follow the Law
image_prompt: The remaining people—priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants, and all who separate themselves to God's law—join their leaders in an oath. They promise not to marry into surrounding peoples' idolatrous practices, not to buy goods on the Sabbath or holy days, and to observe the sabbatical year and remission of debts. Show a public reading of the covenant, households listening, and merchants closing stalls for the Sabbath.

title: Support for the Temple and Its Service
image_prompt: The covenant includes contributions for the service of the house of God, supplies for the offerings, firstfruits, firstborn, tithes, and the promise not to neglect the Temple. Show measured grain, oil, wine, firstfruits, and other contributions brought to store chambers under the supervision of priests and Levites. The final image emphasizes organized, shared responsibility for worship and community care.

title: Families Are Chosen to Live in Jerusalem
image_prompt: The rulers dwell in Jerusalem, and the rest of the people cast lots so that one out of ten will live in the holy city while the others remain in their towns. Some volunteer willingly, and the people bless them. Show families preparing to relocate into Jerusalem's rebuilt neighborhoods, lots being drawn by leaders, and neighbors blessing those who accept the assignment.

title: The Leaders and Families Who Live in Jerusalem
image_prompt: The chapter records the chiefs of Judah and Benjamin living in Jerusalem, including the descendants of Perez, Shelah, Zerah, and Benjamin, along with priests, Levites, gatekeepers, and temple servants. Show an orderly census tableau of families settling into houses and streets near the Temple; include the named officials and the recorder who handles public affairs. Keep the genealogical register central and avoid depicting every named person as part of one gathering.

title: The Surrounding Towns of Judah and Benjamin
image_prompt: The record lists villages and settlements around Jerusalem, from Beer-sheba and the Valley of Hinnom through many towns of Judah, and villages assigned to Benjamin. Present an ancient map on parchment with roads, terraced fields, wells, and small walled towns, while families travel between settlements. The emphasis is the distribution of the returned community across the land.

title: Priests and Levites from the Return to Nehemiah's Day
image_prompt: A genealogical register names priests and Levites who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua, including leaders such as Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra, Amariah, Malluch, Hattush, and many others; later generations and the heads of Levitical families are also recorded. Show the names in generations across a scroll, with small portraits of priests and Levites in service garments and with musical instruments, making clear these are lists spanning years.

title: The People Prepare to Dedicate Jerusalem's Wall
image_prompt: For the wall's dedication, Levites are sought from their places to come to Jerusalem with instruments of thanksgiving—cymbals, psalteries, and harps. Singers gather from nearby villages, purify themselves, the people, the gates, and the wall. Show water and preparations for ritual purification, musicians assembling outside the completed gates, and the repaired ramparts ready for a public celebration.

title: Two Great Processions Celebrate the Wall
image_prompt: Nehemiah arranges two large choirs and processions on top of the wall. One moves toward the Dung Gate and the other in the opposite direction, with leaders, priests, and musicians giving thanks until both reach the house of God. The choirs sing loudly, sacrifices are offered, and the joy of Jerusalem is heard far away. Show two distinct processions on the broad wall, city rooftops filled with onlookers, and musical celebration without modern instruments.

title: Provisions Are Set Aside for Priests and Levites
image_prompt: Men are appointed over store chambers for contributions, firstfruits, and tithes from the fields around the cities. Judah rejoices over the priests and Levites who serve; singers and gatekeepers perform their duties as in David's and Solomon's days. Show store rooms with labeled bins of grain and produce, appointed treasurers keeping records, and priests and Levites receiving their allotted portions.

title: The Law Is Read and the Assembly Separates
image_prompt: The book of Moses is read publicly, and the people hear that the Ammonite and Moabite peoples had not met Israel with bread and water and had hired Balaam to curse them. The assembly applies the law and separates from the mixed religious practices described in the text. Show the public reading of a scroll and a sober gathering responding to covenant instruction, avoiding portrayals of any people as inherently evil.

title: Tobiah's Goods Are Removed from the Temple Chamber
image_prompt: Before this, Eliashib the priest had provided Tobiah a large chamber in the courts of the house of God, a room intended for offerings and sacred supplies. Nehemiah returns to Jerusalem, is distressed, and throws Tobiah's household goods out, then orders the chambers cleansed and the vessels and offerings restored. Show Nehemiah inspecting the chamber, goods carried away, and store rooms purified and restocked.

title: Support for the Levites Is Restored
image_prompt: Nehemiah discovers that the portions for the Levites have not been given, causing the singers and Levites to return to their fields. He rebukes the rulers, restores the provisions, and appoints faithful treasurers over the storehouses. Show Nehemiah questioning officials, Levites returning to service, and measured grain and tithes being distributed fairly.

title: The Sabbath Is Protected
image_prompt: Nehemiah sees people treading winepresses, carrying grain, loading donkeys, and selling fish and goods in Jerusalem on the Sabbath. He rebukes nobles, orders the gates shut before the Sabbath and guarded until it ends, and warns merchants not to camp outside the wall. Levites purify themselves and guard the gates. Show merchants closing stalls, guards at the gates, and the city quiet during sacred rest.

title: Nehemiah Addresses Intermarriage and Final Reforms
image_prompt: Nehemiah finds men who have married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab; he confronts the covenant problem, recalls Solomon's failure, and removes a grandson of Eliashib's family connected to Sanballat from priestly service. He purifies the priesthood and Levites, restores assigned duties, and ensures the wood offering and firstfruits are brought at appointed times. Show a final sequence of Nehemiah correcting household and Temple administration, then praying that God remember his work. Keep family separations and discipline sober rather than sensational.
